post.description: Staff with a confirmed second factor receive a Challenge (no tokens, no cookie) and must call /api/v1/auth/mfa/verify. Web requires an allowed Origin and sets a path-scoped HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie (Secure outside development/test). Mobile requests must have no Origin. Credentials are rate limited by direct peer IP and normalized email: 10 attempts per 15 minutes. No forwarded client IP is trusted. Access lifetime 15 minutes; session hard expiry 7 days.

Set-Cookie.description: Web flow only: spartial_refresh; HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/v1/auth; Secure in production.

post.description: Web uses cookie and exact allowed Origin; mobile sends refresh_token without Origin. Old access token is invalid immediately. Reusing a spent refresh token revokes its entire session, including the latest credentials. Clients must serialize refresh requests, with no automatic retry after ambiguous responses.

post.description: Same Origin/client rules as login. Accepts a TOTP code (each 30-second step usable once, one step of drift) or an unused recovery code. Wrong, reused, expired, exhausted or stale challenges (password/role/suspension changed) return 401 and are audited. Rate limited per IP and per account. Issues an MFA-verified session.

post.description: Pending enrollment expires after ten minutes. Management commands share a ten-attempt per-account 15-minute limit and audit denied factors/reauthentication. Requires password re-authentication. Secret is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted with a configured key bound to the staff id. 409 if a factor is already confirmed; 503 when no encryption keys are configured.

bearerAuth.description: Random 256-bit opaque access credential; hashed server-side, session and live account/permissions checked on each protected request. No JWT algorithm or client-supplied claims.

mfa_verified.description: True only for sessions created after a verified second factor.

access_token.description: Opaque bearer credential, held in browser memory; server checks session on every request.
